I will still do it the way I know from these many years: I start from what worked last year, then I move a little if the crop price or the field condition pushes me. I farm 14 mu by myself, so I cannot spread too wide or do too much fine work on every mu. I will keep the land split across the same five crops, but chili will get more careful feeding because that one brings cash if it stands well. Wheat and cotton I will do steady, not fancy. Garlic and watermelon cost more up front, so I will not plant too much, but I will not starve them either. I use well water, so if the spring is dry I can save the stand. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the plants go yellow and lose yield. What I do mostly comes from my own field and what I see nearby people do when they get a decent harvest. I will plough the crops that like loose soil, use rotary tillage where that is enough, and keep pesticide sprays to the times I usually need, not too few.
